scope: Four displayed storage exterior/cutaway concepts; static only.
actual_inspection: Historical selected storage R5 sheet for preserved geometry and prior authored mechanism distinction
Current canonical resource identity boards and latest passing scale sheets
passing_geometry: Two low utility ports below the left window.
Two rear prepared-food ports at shelf height below the retained round vent.
Front sliding doors and apron remain clear; original right fuel hatch retained.
Food shelf remains above closed raw-food cabinets; no front aisle converted into a belt.
Exterior approaches have supporting frames and end plates; current R1 conveyor color family retained.

defects.finding: External utility sleeves and the two internal trays are shown, but the path across the wall is not visibly traceable to the corresponding internal tray. The fixed vertical lift has a separated handoff to the rack; no supported lateral transfer bridge or indexed shelf landing is shown.
defects.repair: Use a local cutaway/closeup or bounded edit that exposes the sleeve-to-tray supports and a supported short lateral bridge/transfer position between lift and selected shelf. Preserve facade, four ports and floor access. Do not hide the connection behind an inferred tunnel or unsupported gap.
defects.claim_limit: This is missing visual interface evidence, not a claim that every conceivable unseen mechanism is impossible.

defects.finding: Generic small gray cube piles and generic orange tray morsels replace identifiable approved mineral/processed-food tokens. These were historical illustration conventions; they are not the current resource identity proof.
defects.repair: Keep the existing carrier trays if needed, but put recognizable approved wood/mineral/block and food units in them, with type labels where necessary and no shrink-to-fit. Preserve raw/processed distinctions and individual variant size through each handoff.

defects.finding: The required utility receiving-full/held state is not shown; the normal two wood bundles alone do not prove a visibly held inlet.
defects.repair: Add a finite full receiving tray with its upstream stop visibly closed, in a state inset or additional sheet.

food_shuttle_note: The shelf-height rail and local carriage are visible. Clear approved goods and request/held state evidence are still needed for the mapped scope; an illustration does not prove scheduling or no-loop control.
next_action: Target internal handoff visibility, canonical contents and the missing receiving-held inset; retest all affected panels.
